key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even when deep defect levels are present, both nonradiative and radiative SRH recombination remain too weak to explain the observed photovoltaic losses.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, with defect engineering likely less critical than in many other emerging materials.
method: First-principles calculations of point defects in trigonal selenium
Large, chemically diverse defect dataset spanning multiple charge states and defect levels
Evaluation of defect-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall recombination via nonradiative multiphonon and radiative capture pathways
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a broad first-principles survey showing large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per recombination event, which strongly suppress defect-assisted SRH recombination.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on calculated defect physics, so device performance can still depend on defect populations, microstructure, and extrinsic losses not captured by point-defect models alone.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
